title: Fiber-seq for Flash Frozen Mouse Gastroc Tissue for IGVF
author: Jasmine Sakr
materials: Make enough Buffers for the total number of samples and keep on ice. steps.title: Keep tissue on dry ice
steps.instruction: Store flash‑frozen mouse gastroc tissue on dry ice until the lysis step begins.

steps.title: Spin nuclei sample
steps.instruction: Spin 3 × 10⁶ nuclei at 500 × g, 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Set thermomixers
steps.instruction: Set one thermomixer to 56 °C and a second thermomixer to 25 °C.

steps.title: Prepare extraction tubes
steps.instruction: Label the following tubes for each labeling reaction: bead strainer in a collection tube, 2 mL tube for wash step, 2 mL tube for elution step, 1.5 mL tube for final elution. Add 100 µL gDNA Elution Buffer II to each 2 mL elution tube.

steps.title: Prepare ice bucket reagents
steps.instruction: Place Proteinase K, RNase A (0.5 M), and Spermidine on ice in a bucket.

steps.title: Add extraction buffer
steps.instruction: Add 2.5 mL Nuclei Extraction Buffer to a chilled gentleMACS C Tube.

steps.title: Add frozen tissue
steps.instruction: Drop the whole frozen tissue into the chilled gentleMACS C Tube containing the 2.5 mL Nuclei Extraction Buffer.

steps.title: Invert and load dissociator
steps.instruction: Immediately invert the tube to prevent tissue from sticking to the bottom or sides, then load it onto the Octo Dissociator and place an Octo Cooler over the tube.

steps.title: Run gentleMACS program
steps.instruction: Run the gentleMACS program 4C_nuclei_1 on the Octo Dissociator for 00:05:00.

steps.title: Check dissociation and repeat if needed
steps.instruction: Remove the gentleMACS C Tube and tap to ensure tissue is not stuck. If dissociation fails, repeat the program up to three times. After the third failure, transfer tissue to a new 1.5 mL tube, place at –80 °C for 5–10 minutes to refreeze, then retry.

steps.title: Brief spin
steps.instruction: Spin the tube in a 4 °C centrifuge for 00:00:10 (10 seconds).

steps.title: Mix nuclei suspension
steps.instruction: Gently and thoroughly mix the nuclei suspension by pipetting with a 5 mL pipette.

steps.title: Filter through 70 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Filter the nuclei suspension through a 70 µm MACS SmartStrainer into a 5 mL tube. Hold the 5 mL pipette perpendicular to the filter, press the tip against the centre, and slowly pass the suspension while moving the tip in a small circular motion.

steps.title: Wash used C tube
steps.instruction: Add an additional 2 mL Nuclei Extraction Buffer to the empty, used gentleMACS C Tube, close the cap, and swish to recover any nuclei stuck to the sides.

steps.title: Filter wash buffer
steps.instruction: Filter the 2 mL additional Nuclei Extraction Buffer through the same 70 µm MACS SmartStrainer into the same 5 mL tube (total volume now ≈ 4.5 mL).

steps.title: Centrifuge nuclei suspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 4.5 mL nuclei suspension at 700 × g, 4 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully discard the supernatant without disturbing the nuclei pellet.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in RSB
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclei pellet in 3.1 mL RSB. Pipette up and down 7–10 times with a 5 mL pipette.

steps.title: Filter through 30 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Filter the nuclei suspension through a 30 µm MACS SmartStrainer into a 15 mL tube.

steps.title: Aliquot nuclei for labeling
steps.instruction: Make aliquots of 3 × 10⁶ nuclei in 1.5 mL tubes and proceed to labeling and DNA extraction.

steps.title: Prepare reaction master mix
steps.instruction: During the 5‑minute spin, mix Buffer A with Spermidine (room temperature) and keep the Reaction Master Mix on ice.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei in master mix
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and resuspend the nuclei pellet in 180 µL Reaction Master Mix.

steps.title: Incubate labeling reaction
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube on a 25 °C heat block for 00:10:00.

steps.title: Add DNA capture beads
steps.instruction: Add 2 DNA capture beads to each sample.

steps.title: Add isopropanol
steps.instruction: Calculate and add 0.7 × volume isopropanol to each sample.

steps.title: Mix to bind DNA
steps.instruction: Mix on a vertical rotating mixer at 10 rpm for 10 minutes to attach DNA to the beads.

steps.title: Wash beads – first discard
steps.instruction: Keep the tube upright, insert a pipette tip, gently push the beads aside, and discard the liquid.

steps.title: Wash beads – first buffer
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Wash Buffer and gently invert the tube 3 times.

steps.title: Wash beads – second discard
steps.instruction: Keep the tube upright, insert a pipette tip, gently push the beads aside, and discard the liquid.

steps.title: Wash beads – second buffer
steps.instruction: Add another 500 µL Wash Buffer and gently invert the tube 3 times.

steps.title: Wash beads – third discard
steps.instruction: Keep the tube upright, insert a pipette tip, gently push the beads aside, and discard the liquid.

steps.title: Transfer beads to retainer
steps.instruction: Pour the beads into the bead retainer that sits in a collection tube.

steps.title: Pulse spin beads
steps.instruction: Pulse‑spin (≤ 1 second) the tubes to remove any residual wash buffer from the beads.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Separate the bead retainer from the collection tube, pour the beads into a labeled tube containing 100 µL elution buffer, and keep the bead retainer for a later step.

steps.title: Incubate elution
steps.instruction: Incubate on a thermal mixer at 56 °C for 00:10:00. After the first 5 minutes, tilt the tube almost horizontally and gently shake to expose all bead surfaces to the elution buffer.

steps.title: Final DNA incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the DNA by one of the following methods: 37 °C for 01:00:00 or 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Collect eluate with glass beads
steps.instruction: Pour the eluate and the glass beads into the bead retainer placed in the final labeled tube.

steps.title: Separate eluate from glass beads
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 12 000 rpm, 25 °C for 30 seconds to separate eluate from the glass beads.

steps.title: Mix eluate gently
steps.instruction: Mix gently by pipetting using a wide‑bore tip.

steps.title: ONT library preparation
steps.instruction: Follow the Oxford Nanopore Technologies "ONT Library Prep for Whole Genome Sequencing" protocol to build sequencing libraries.

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration of each tube with a Qubit fluorometer, keep tubes on ice until library prep or store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Add DRS and mix
steps.instruction: Add 900 µL DRS to each tube and mix by pipetting 10 times slowly up and down using a 5 mL pipette.

steps.title: Overlay with PBS
steps.instruction: Overlay each tube with 4 mL PBS using a P1000 or P5000 pipette. Place the tube on a flat surface, tilt it 45°, add the first 1 mL slowly, then increase the addition speed for the remaining volume.

steps.title: Centrifuge nuclei suspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 3000 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes with no brake. Three phases will form: top transparent buffer, middle cloudy debris band, bottom transparent nuclei layer.

steps.title: Aspirate top phases
steps.instruction: Aspirate and discard the top buffer layer and the middle cloudy debris band (≈ 1000 µL total) while staying above the nuclei layer. Approximately 2000 µL of nuclei‑containing suspension remains.

steps.title: Adjust final volume with RSB
steps.instruction: Add cold RSB to the remaining suspension until the total volume reaches 5 mL. Gently invert the tube three times; do NOT vortex.

steps.title: Prepare nuclei extraction tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare and label for each sample: a pre‑chilled gentleMACS C Tube, a 5 mL tube, a 15 mL tube, 70 µm MACS SmartStrainer, 30 µm MACS SmartStrainer, and a disposable hemacytometer.

steps.title: Centrifuge nuclei pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 1000 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes with full brake.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei for counting
steps.instruction: Fully resuspend the nuclei pellet in 187.5 µL RSB.

steps.title: Count nuclei
steps.instruction: Dilute 2 µL of the suspension with 20 µL dye (1:11 dilution). Mix 7–10 times, load 10 µL onto a disposable hemacytometer, and count nuclei. If counts from two opposite squares differ greatly, count a third square and use the most consistent value.

steps.title: Incubate beads after SDS
steps.instruction: Incubate for 01:00:00 at room temperature, tilting the tube almost horizontally and gently shaking every 5 minutes to keep all bead surfaces exposed to elution buffer.

steps.title: Add SDS to samples
steps.instruction: Add 20 % SDS to each sample to achieve a final concentration of 1 % (calculate the required volume). Add the SDS dropwise with a pipette tip, moving the tip after each drop to avoid bubbles.

steps.title: Mix after SDS addition
steps.instruction: Thoroughly mix by gently inverting the tube; do NOT vortex or pipette. If DNA will be extracted later, flash‑freeze and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Transfer upper DNA phase
steps.instruction: Using a wide‑bore tip, transfer as much of the upper phase containing DNA to a labeled empty 2 mL tube without disturbing the pellet. Record the total transferred volume for later steps.

steps.title: Mix on rotating mixer
steps.instruction: Mix on a vertical rotating mixer at 20 rpm for 1 minute.

steps.title: Add protein separation solution
steps.instruction: Add 180 µL Protein Separation solution to each tube.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 16 000 × g, 25 °C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Thermal mixer incubation with enzymes
steps.instruction: Incubate in a thermal mixer at 2000 rpm, 56 °C for 10 minutes. If starting from a thawed reaction, first add 20 µL Proteinase K and 10 µL RNase A to each tube and mix with a wide‑bore tip. Skip this addition if the lysate will be frozen for later DNA extraction.

steps.title: Add Proteinase K and RNase A (optional)
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL Proteinase K and 10 µL RNase A to each tube and mix using a wide‑bore pipette tip. *Skip this step if you plan to freeze the lysate and extract DNA later.
